pass_b_english: Cyril: …honor and glory truly for the sacred and holy race is Christ, a bright and beyond-world adornment for the souls of the saints. ‘For as many as into Christ you were baptized, Christ you put on,’ (Galatians 3:27) he says, and true is the word. And as in shadows the law beautifies Aaron, carrying up unto Christ the glory from having been dressed many-formedly. For all but also woven-together with the construction of the craft-works a mystical and exact word is found, showing riddlingly the glory of the Savior. For see how he says the craftsmen of the garments have been filled with the understanding from God, carrying them unto flower-bright embroidery, and writing the glory of Christ into the robes. And breastpiece and shoulder-piece, and foot-reaching robe, and the tasseled tunic, and headdress and belt, the things being crafted, these and in addition to them others, which also part by part for us, as possible, will be said. So then he said concerning those taken into the works, ‘And they will take the gold, and the hyacinth, and the purple, and the scarlet, and linen.’ (Exodus 28:5–7) And again casting a thin mind into the things set forth for me, and before at least the others observe this.
Palladius: What sort of thing do you say?
Cyril: For have not of gold and linen, and indeed also purple and spun scarlet, and hyacinth again all the things in the tent been made, and it was unto a type of Christ?

Cyril: And see that through the same also the stole of the one excelling in priesthood has been arranged, travailing the glory of Christ as again in an image and types; for the same words, and not another knowledge, signify the beauty of Christ. For he is known as in gold God, as in purple having the kingly dignity, and as in fine linen a thin and bodiless word, as in scarlet through the flesh; and in air-appearing hyacinth—for such-colored is hyacinth—through the from-above and from heaven. Or is not the Word from God Father both God together and king?
Cyril: And being Word of the Father thin and bodiless, has he not come to be in flesh and is he from above?

Cyril: So then the same materials indistinguishably and as in thin contemplation both of the garments, and indeed also of the things constructed in the holy tent. And these things thus; and the things unto honor and glory for Aaron many-formedly woven it is already time to say. So then, ‘And they will make,’ (John 1:14) he says, ‘the shoulder-piece from spun linen, a woven work of an embroiderer, two shoulder-pieces holding together will be for him, one the other upon the two parts having been hung.
